system.name: RegenHance
system.one_liner: a region-based content enhancement system for efficient video analytics at the edge, using profile-based execution planning across heterogeneous hardware

content.subject: how RegenHance profiles DFG components across hardware, then dynamic-programs a CPU/GPU execution schedule meeting performance targets

content.key_idea: RegenHance plans execution for a multi-model video-analytics pipeline in four steps: express the task as a dataflow graph, profile every component's throughput on every available hardware unit at different batch sizes, run a dynamic-programming search over these profiles to meet a latency/accuracy target, and realize the result as a concrete CPU/GPU schedule.
content.reading_order: left to right through the four circled steps: ① the DFG, ② its profiling table, ③ the dynamic-programming search producing an Exec Plan, ④ the resulting CPU/GPU schedule timeline

evidence: Our crucial choice is to assign each component’s input tensor size
Batching execution, i.e., grouping input matrices into one, is well known to achieve high processor utilization by DNNs
it also allows the inference engines to achieve various throughputs by adjusting different batch sizes

summary: Figure 12 walks through RegenHance's profile-based execution planning for a 7-stream, <1s-latency/>0.9-accuracy workload on one CPU plus one GPU. Step ① expresses the analytical task as a dataflow graph (Decode, Importance Pred., Region Enhan., Semantic Seg., Obj. Det.). Step ② profiles every component on every hardware option at several batch sizes, recording batch size (Bat), time cost (Cos) and throughput (TPS) in a Model@HW table. Step ③ runs a dynamic-programming search over these profiles to pick a batch size and hardware assignment (Exec Plan) meeting the target latency and accuracy. Step ④ realizes that plan as a concrete schedule: the CPU alternates Decode/Importance-Prediction blocks while the GPU runs Region-Enhancement/Segmentation/Detection blocks. A consistent colour per component runs through the DFG, the profiling table's row bands, and the final schedule blocks, letting a reader trace one component across all four stages.
